policy_context.execution_authorization_reference: Current explicit owner instruction 2026-10-22 authorizes bounded exploratory M4 measurements and remeasurement after material instrumentation changes, using fresh operation IDs and full containment; no retry after a gate failure and no hard-gate bypass.
policy_context.resource_basis: Distinct, one-shot paired experiment following the direct flush-staging pair: compare ordinary Upsert against bounded four-record/500-us Upsert group commit while both arms use metadata staging, the same 8,192-document corpus, default compaction, two readers, 32 logical writes, WAL fsync, explicit flush and reopen/replay checks. During each arm, retain the established concurrent-reader/compaction phase and then run continuous timestamped readers across explicit Flush; require at least two completed queries per reader before and after plus a query starting and overlapping the native flush interval, corroborated by M4_PHASE events. Capture writer wall/state wait and group size/queue delay/fsyncs, reader total wall/native mutex wait/execution CPU for concurrent compaction and explicit flush, flush stage/query-lock/state-lock timings, bytes, cgroup/host resource and I/O evidence. Both arms keep atomic visibility and durability unchanged; group commit remains default-off. This is a new cross-factor comparison, not a retry of the consumed direct-vs-staging profile. Any gate, containment or overlap failure consumes this profile without retry. Exploratory only; not qualification, stable-tail claim, architecture win, or production authorization.
policy_context.risk_acceptance_reference: The standard contention profile is four-arm; writer_group_commit is a separate two-arm per-call Upsert experiment. All are descriptive only: shared-host pressure, one round per arm and test-scale workloads prohibit causal, qualification or architecture-win claims. ApplyBatch and Upsert call latencies have different units and must not be compared as equivalent tail samples.
